What was read

All 3,748 publicly posted/indexed comments in the October 21, 2026 inventory. The reading unit was one representative per form-letter cluster, every unclustered comment, the novel text of every clustered copy (word-level diff against its representative; 1,305 copies had added text), and every readable attachment in full (174 attachment texts). 3,642 of 3,748 comments are covered by at least one extracted recommendation, directly or as a copy of a cited representative. The other 106 contain no actionable ask (personal narrative only, general opposition, or an attachment with no ask).

Unreadable or non-substantive attachments

  • No text (photographs): CDC-2026-1387-0415, -0735, -2398 (two files).
  • OCR unreadable: -2128.
  • Copies of the Federal Register notice only: -1868, -1893, -1902. Unrelated 2021 op-ed: -1987.
  • Evidence only, no further asks: -2936 (published Long COVID studies), -3437 (the commenter's NHIS-based COPD papers), -3171 (arts-and-health fact sheet).
  • Comment -2943 reproduces comment -2645; their duplicate wording is counted once for recommendation-text screening, while both public comment records remain in the full 3,748-submission corpus.

Volume columns (kept out of the score)

  • Comments: distinct comment IDs that carry the ask (body, attachment, or personalized addition).
  • Letters: same, but each form-letter cluster counts once.
  • Incl. copies: adds every member of a cluster whose representative carries the ask. This assumes copies endorse the template's asks.

Scoring rubric (1–5 each; total 5–25)

Dimension5 means1 means
SpecificityNames item/variable and the concrete change or wordingGeneral sentiment
Evidence / expertiseCites data, studies or statute, or comes from a source with direct expertise in the measureAssertion only
ConsequenceLoss or gain affects a core estimate, a statutory or HP2030 use, or a trend seriesMarginal analytic effect
FeasibilityLow burden, works in web and paper modes, item already fieldedLarge redesign, costly, or not survey-appropriate
NoveltyA point few or no other commenters raisedWidely repeated point

Must-review = specificity ≥ 4 or evidence ≥ 4 (142 of 201 issues). Scores are issue-level AI judgments, not averages of per-comment scores.

Spot-check (20 random recommendations)

All 1,464 quotes passed an automated verbatim check: NFKC/quote-normalized substring of the comment body plus attachment text, and no more than 40 words. Twenty records drawn at random (seed 20261024) were then re-read against their source context.

  • Quote verbatim and correctly attributed: 20/20.
  • Substantive misclassification: 1/20 (5%). In -2345 (UCSF), an ask to keep smoking history, cessation and alcohol in the core was filed under the H3 binge-drinking issue. It has been moved to I-147.
  • Minor: 2/20. A request from -0022 to publish test results sits under the disability-identification testing issue, when the documentation issue would fit better. The quote for -2272 expresses the wish to be counted, not the ask itself.
  • Error rate: 5% substantive, 15% including minor.

Known limits

  • Submitter type is inferred from the organization field and the text.
  • Some PDF-extracted attachments have broken hyphenation or spacing. Quotes avoid those spans.
  • Commenters' own figures are reported as their claims and were not verified against the draft (e.g., -3749: "removes over 330 questions out of 482"). One comment (-2755, ACS/ACS CAN) says the draft lacks disability status. The WG-SS is in draft Section C.
  • Issue groupings and titles are editorial. Use the Recommendations tab to see the underlying asks.
